beats.narration: Three doors. One prize. Pick a door.

beats.text:
The host knows.
One empty door opens.
beats.narration: The host knows where it is. They always open another, empty door.
Switching wins whenever your first pick is wrong. That's two out of three.
We played it again and again. Here's what happened.

sources.claim: Switching wins two thirds of games when the host knows the prize location, always opens a different losing door and always offers the switch.
sources.ref: Steve Selvin, On the Monty Hall Problem (1975), The American Statistician. https://www.montyhallproblem.com/as.html

post.caption:
You pick a door. The host knows where the prize is and always opens another door that's empty. Then you're offered a switch. Would you take it?

Switching wins whenever your first pick misses. That happens two times out of three.
